🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin and Ether slid over 3% as ETF outflows resumed and a $70M wallet exploit rattled self-custody confidence. Yet institutional plumbing kept advancing, with Circle's new trust charter and a Senate push on the CLARITY Act. 🔓 Coldcard Wallet Exploit Grows to $70M, CZ Urges Diversification A firmware flaw in Coinkite's Coldcard hardware wallets let an attacker reconstruct supposedly random seed phrases, draining roughly 1,000 BTC (about $70 million) from 1,196 wallets in a 41-minute window on July 30 — nearly double the amount first reported. Binance founder CZ urged holders to split funds across multiple wallets, reviving debate over the limits of self-custody. Read full story → ⚖️ Grayscale, Strategy Press Senate to Pass CLARITY Act With Congress set to break for its August recess, Grayscale sent Senate leaders an urgent letter demanding a floor vote on the CLARITY Act, and bitcoin treasury firm Strategy publicly backed the bill hours later. The market-structure bill has cleared the House and the Senate Banking Committee but still has no floor vote scheduled. More details → 📉 Bitcoin ETFs Shed $265M as BlackRock's IBIT Leads Redemptions US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $265.4 million in net outflows on July 31, ending a brief two-day return to inflows. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $122.7 million of the exodus, followed by Fidelity's FBTC and Grayscale's GBTC, as institutional sentiment turned cautious heading into August. See details → 💵 Tether Posts $1.5B Q2 Profit, Reserve Buffer Halves Tether reported $1.5 billion in net operating profit for the second quarter, driven by Treasury and repo returns, even as its excess reserve buffer fell from $8.23 billion to $4.11 billion on unrealized bitcoin and gold losses. The stablecoin giant added 14 tons of gold and roughly 1,800 BTC to its holdings. Read more → 🏛️ Circle Wins New York Trust Charter for USDC USDC issuer Circle secured a limited-purpose trust charter from New York's financial regulator, allowing it to offer fiduciary and custody services under state banking law. The approval follows Circle's national trust bank approval from the OCC earlier this month, deepening its push into regulated institutional custody.
